subject: High p99/TTFT spikes — investigation pointing to CDN/TLS handshake delays
messages:
From: Jake Moreno <ops@atlashealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p99 TTFT spikes across our production traffic

Monica,

We're seeing a sharp increase in first-token latency (TTFT) and p99 spikes on the hosted API over the last 90 minutes. This started around 08:05 PT and is impacting our user logins and initial-response heatmap. Overall throughput hasn't dropped much, but the TTFT jump is causing client-side timeouts and poor UX.

Short summary of what we observe from our side:
- p95 went from ~180ms to 420ms; p99 jumped to 1.2s+
- Error rate for init requests rose from 0.2% to 1.8% (mainly client timeouts)
- Impacted region: us-west, but traffic is global

We collected a trace and attached a .har and some TLS debug logs. Can you triage? We're in a live environment and would appreciate an internal ETA and any mitigations.

Thanks,
Jake
Ops Lead — Atlas Health

Attachments: atlas-trace-ttft.har, tls-debug.log
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jake Moreno <ops@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 TTFT spikes across our production traffic

Hi Jake — thanks for the quick heads up and for attaching the traces.

I've looped in our SRE (Dev) to triage immediately. Initial ask: can you confirm whether affected requests are hitting our hosted endpoints directly or via FastEdge CDN? Any recent config changes on your side?

We will update within 30 minutes.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 TTFT spikes across our production traffic

Monica / team — I pulled the uploaded traces (thanks Jake). Quick triage notes:

- The spans show excessive TLS handshake times at the edge (SYN/TLS) before our first token is emitted. Median handshake time is normal but tail is high (300–900ms).
- The requests in question appear to ingress via FastEdge POPs in us-west. The path then routes to our hosted API layer (model-serving cluster).
- Our runtime reports per-token generation latency is unchanged once the request reaches the model instance; increase is in pre-service phase (TTFT).

I opened a support ticket with FastEdge (ticket 78921) and attached a compressed set of handshake traces (handshake-traces-20260415.zip). FastEdge has acknowledged similar reports from other customers in the same POP.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing:
1) Bypass FastEdge for Atlas Health traffic (route direct to our ingest LB) while we validate — this is a DNS/route change and can be done for their IP blocks.
2) Add short-term client-side retry logic with jitter (advised for timeouts) — ask Atlas to enable if possible.
3) If DNS switch is risky, add a temporary stickier path to a different FastEdge POP with healthy TLS metrics.

I'll continue to coordinate with FastEdge and update. If leadership wants to weigh in on DNS bypass (exec sign-off required for persistent routing changes), please advise.

—Dev
Dev Patel
SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachment: handshake-traces-20260415.zip
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p99 TTFT spikes across our production traffic

Rishi / Sean — forwarding a high-severity customer escalation (Atlas Health). Initial triage from SRE indicates upstream TLS handshake tail at a FastEdge POP is the likely root cause of first-token latency regressions.

Why this needs exec attention:
- Atlas is a top-20 customer with platform calls in several v1 products; impact is user-visible and affecting renewals conversation.
- Proposed mitigation (DNS bypass for their traffic) is low-risk on paper but requires leadership sign-off for a manual routing exception and cross-team coordination (network, infra, legal).
- We should determine whether to apply a broader traffic steering policy to avoid fragile POPs (may affect cost/contract with CDN partner).

Asks:
- Rishi: can you approve a short-lived route bypass if SRE recommends it?
- Sean: can you align with partnerships/legal on whether we can request a contractual escalation with FastEdge for SLA credits and diagnostics?

I'll keep Atlas updated and will only apply changes after we confirm the plan.

—Monica
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 TTFT spikes across our production traffic

Thanks for the signal and the clear mitigation plan. Approve proceeding with a targeted DNS bypass for Atlas Health IP blocks for up to 12 hours while we validate end-to-end.

Operational notes from me:
- Dev: implement the bypass and monitor p95/p99 and error rate; if we see improvements, keep route for another 12–24h and then consider a traffic-steering rule (server-side) to avoid that FastEdge POP for similar customers.
- If the bypass reduces latency but FastEdge doesn't provide timely remediation, we should discuss switching to an alternate partner POP at scale or using our multi-CDN steering rules.
- Sean: please escalate contract/SLA ask with FastEdge; ask for diagnostic logs and an RCA timeline.

I'll be available on standby for exec decisions.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Platform Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jake Moreno <ops@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Update: TTFT/p99 incident — temporary routing applied and status

Jake — quick update and apology for the disruption. We performed a targeted DNS route bypass for Atlas Health traffic late this morning (approved by Rishi). Post-bypass observations:

- p95 returned to ~170–200ms; p99 down to ~350–420ms (close to expected baseline)
- Error rate for initial requests dropped back to 0.3%
- No observable change in model-serving latency (confirms pre-service handshake was the issue)

FastEdge has acknowledged a degraded POP and opened an internal RCA; they have shared interim diagnostics and are working on a remediation patch. We're continuing to monitor and will keep the bypass in place for 24 hours while we validate stability.

Next steps for Atlas (what we recommend):
1) Keep retry-with-jitter enabled on client SDKs for the next 48 hours; we can push a minor client-config change if you want.
2) We'll share the FastEdge ticket and post-RCA once available.
3) If you prefer not to route via bypass, we can revert and coordinate a live test with FastEdge to prove fix before reattaching.

Really appreciate the quick signal and patience — please reach out if you see any regressions.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
